mcqs.question: Consider the sets A = {1,2,3} and B = {a,b,c}. The relation R = {(1,a), (2,b), (3,a)} is to be shown with a diagram. Which diagram correctly represents R?

options.A: Arrows from 1 to a, 2 to b, and 3 to a.
options.B: Arrows from 1 to b, 2 to a, and 3 to c.
options.C: Arrows from 1 to a, 2 to a, and 3 to b.
options.D: Arrows from 1 to c, 2 to b, and 3 to a.

mcqs.answer: Arrows from 1 to a, 2 to b, and 3 to a.
mcqs.explanation: A relation is a set of ordered pairs. For each pair (x,y) we draw an arrow from the element x in set A to the element y in set B. The pairs (1,a), (2,b) and (3,a) give exactly the arrows described in option A. The other options show different pairings that are not in R.

mcqs.question: Let S = {(x, y) | x ∈ {−2, 0, 2, 4}, y = x²}. What is the domain of the relation S?
mcqs.explanation: The domain consists of all first components of the ordered pairs. Since the relation is defined for each x in the set {−2,0,2,4}, the domain is exactly that set. Option B lists the second components (the squares), and C and D miss some elements.

mcqs.question: For the relation T = {(p,q) | p ∈ {a,b,c}, q ∈ {1,2} and q = 1 if p = a or b, q = 2 if p = c}, what is the range of T?
mcqs.explanation: The range (or image) is the set of all second components that actually appear. In T the second component is 1 for a and b, and 2 for c, so the range is {1,2}. Option A is the domain, while C and D mix elements from both sets.

mcqs.question: Given the relation U = {(1,α), (2,β), (3,α)} where the first set X = {1,2,3} and the second set Y = {α,β,γ}, which set is the codomain of U?
mcqs.explanation: The codomain is the set from which the second elements of ordered pairs are taken, i.e., the whole set Y. Even though γ does not appear in the relation, it is still part of the codomain. Options A, C, and D omit elements of Y.

mcqs.question: Let A be the set of students and B the set of subjects. Define R as “student studies subject”. Which of the following statements correctly defines the relation R?

options.A: Each student is assigned exactly one subject.
options.B: R is the set of ordered pairs (student, subject) such that the student studies the subject.
options.C: R is a function from subjects to students.
options.D: R is a mapping that assigns a grade to each student.

mcqs.answer: R is the set of ordered pairs (student, subject) such that the student studies the subject.
mcqs.explanation: A relation between two sets is precisely a collection of ordered pairs taken from the Cartesian product of the sets. Option B states this definition. Option A adds a restriction (exactly one) that is not required for a general relation. Option C reverses the direction, and D describes a different concept (a function assigning grades).

mcqs.question: In a school, the set of teachers T = {Mr. A, Ms. B} and the set of classes C = {Class 1, Class 2, Class 3}. The relation “teacher teaches class” consists of Mr. A teaching Class 1 and Class 3, and Ms. B teaching Class 2. Which set of ordered pairs correctly represents this relation?

options.A: {(Mr. A, Class 1), (Mr. A, Class 3), (Ms. B, Class 2)}
options.B: {(Class 1, Mr. A), (Class 3, Mr. A), (Class 2, Ms. B)}
options.C: {(Mr. A, Class 2), (Ms. B, Class 1), (Ms. B, Class 3)}
options.D: {(Mr. A, Class 1), (Ms. B, Class 1), (Ms. B, Class 3)}

mcqs.answer: {(Mr. A, Class 1), (Mr. A, Class 3), (Ms. B, Class 2)}
mcqs.explanation: The ordered pair (teacher, class) records which teacher is linked to which class. Option A lists exactly the three teaching assignments described. Option B swaps the order of the pair, option C lists wrong pairings, and option D adds a non‑existent teaching link (Ms. B to Class 1).

mcqs.question: Statement: “In a relation diagram, if an element of set A is connected to more than one element of set B, the relation is not a function.” Which option correctly identifies the misconception in this statement?

options.A: The statement is true; such a diagram cannot represent a relation.
options.B: The statement confuses the definition of a relation with that of a function; a relation may have multiple arrows from an element.
options.C: The statement is true only when the codomain consists of a single element.
options.D: The statement is false because relations cannot be represented by diagrams.

mcqs.answer: The statement confuses the definition of a relation with that of a function; a relation may have multiple arrows from an element.
mcqs.explanation: A relation is any subset of the Cartesian product, so an element of the first set can be related to many elements of the second set. The restriction that each element of the first set be linked to at most one element defines a *function*, not a general relation. Hence option B points out the misconception. Options A and C incorrectly treat the statement as true, and D is wrong because relations are routinely drawn as arrow diagrams.

mcqs.question: The relation V = {(m, n) | m ∈ {1,2,3,4}, n = m + 1}. Which set is the domain of V, and why?

options.A: {2, 3, 4, 5} because the second component is m+1.
options.B: {1, 2, 3, 4} because the domain consists of all possible first components m.
options.C: {0, 1, 2, 3} because subtracting 1 from each ordered pair gives the domain.
options.D: {1, 3, 5, 7} because only odd numbers appear as first components.

mcqs.answer: {1, 2, 3, 4} because the domain consists of all possible first components m.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, the domain of a relation is the set of all first elements of its ordered pairs. Here the first element m can be any of {1,2,3,4}, independent of the rule for n. Therefore the domain is exactly {1,2,3,4}. Option A mistakenly lists the second components, C gives an incorrect transformation, and D is unrelated.
